stem.text: Determine whether the power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n} \left(x - 1\right)^{n}}{3^{n} n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \) converges or diverges at the right endpoint of its interval of convergence, naming the test used.

answer_key.label: At \( x = 4 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \) decrease to 0.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 1\right| < 3 \), so the right endpoint is \( x = 4 \).
At \( x = 4 \), \( \frac{\left(x - 1\right)^{n}}{3^{n}} = \left(\frac{3}{3}\right)^{n} = 1 \), so the series becomes \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n}}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \).
The terms alternate in sign, their sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \) decrease as n increases, and \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} = 0 \).
At \( x = 4 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{n^{\frac{3}{2}}} \) decrease to 0, so \( x = 4 \) belongs to the interval of convergence.
